This does not feel like a deckbuilder. And the overall feel of the game is not good. The tag and the reviews deceived me hard.

EDIT: since posting this review, a lot of the criticism I had has been addressed and fixed by the developer. The game was already good but now it's shaping up to be amazing! Great work! TL;DR good space card game. Strange mix of deckbuilding and Faster Than Light visuals. Good atmosphere. Great music. Some bugs and a few questionable design decisions. Terrible English voice acting. Yes, overall I recommend the game HOWEVER there's a few things to say about it. At the time of writing, it feels like it's at an early stage of development, despite the fact that it technically just released. For example, one time I tried stealing from pirates, got caught, talked my way out of it, got a perk for it, then stole something else from them, didn't get caught, however it turned out to be faulty equipment which automatically replaced my newly acquired perk with a negative one. I immediately tried stealing a third thing and lo and behold, I instantly got rid of the negative perk and acquired back the one I had just lost. Right after, an NPC offered to get rid of the negative perk I had just replaced (and no longer had). To top it all, I somehow ended up with more health than my maximum would allow, until the game forced me to "repair" my ship for free and set me back to my maximum. What. Before moving on from the stealing bit, the very first time I did it I apparently triggered a different event where the merchant scams me, keeps the money and runs away. However, because I stole the item, none of it made sense. The dialogue said I had "spent money" (I didn't) and the merchant was still there afterwards. It was very confusing. The English voice acting, while I admit has some style and does grow on you, sounds absolutely atrocious due to the sheer level of mispronunciations and there's a large number of typos that can be noticed in the text. The tutorial DOES NOT adequately prepare you for the game at all because it only focuses on the combat side of things, which is only one aspect of the game and literally tells you "hover over anything you want to know" which doesn't help much when every card has a million keywords whose explanation can only be read outside of combat. There's a long, comprehensive (yet not comprehensive enough in my opinion) codex to help you out but if I wanted a manual I wouldn't have clicked on tutorial. Your best way to learn is by trial and error through gameplay as there's too much text to get into it quickly like you could with Slay the Spire. There's an RPG element to your character and stats that level up depending on your actions which (I believe) influence the outcome of certain events. However, when compared to a game like Faster Than Light (which the game itself clearly took inspiration from in its presentation), you'll notice how it has a strict 1 combat policy per jump, meaning that if you run into certain events that are hostile (such as stealing from pirates and getting caught), you can never get into a battle as a result and you will ALWAYS talk your way out of it, worst case scenario trading some resources or acquiring a new perk. It kinda pulls you out of it when you keep clicking the most dangerous and questionable choices available to you and keep getting away with it. It seems like the only downside is your equipment getting damaged or you losing some currency. The game should also provide some numbers on screen when they matter, such as when making a dialogue choice based on my character's stats, it would be helpful if they were displayed when hovering over said decision to help me assess it better. Speaking of perks, they are meant to represent the progression of your character and the consequences of your actions but there's only 5 slots for them. You will quickly run out and the game will ask if you want to replace an old one for a new one, which you can always decline, making your actions feel unimpactful to your character. Your deck starts with 10 cards, however the minimum is 6 so the first thing you do every run if you're familiar with deckbuilding games is remove 4 of them. You don't even lose them, just set them aside. This is counterintuitive design, you should either start with the minimum number of cards allowed or there should be a downside to removing them, otherwise it's just busywork. A few small things: some hitboxes should be corrected, for example the correct spot to hover the cards you want to steal is very finnicky and there's no confirmation dialogue when stealing is successful. Every time I do it I have to pay close attention to my currency. The ship's log is actually useful but it fills with information so fast you always have to scroll back up to read it all and "auto scroll" is ALWAYS enabled even if you tried disabling it previously. Every time I jump I have to uncheck auto scroll and then scroll back up. How about a button that expands it instead? Finally, you learn through gameplay that enemies come to you in waves. I was breezing through the levels with a loadout I liked when I finally faced the boss. Turns out, you have to go to the boss. The only card in my deck that allowed my ship to move forward was also the only card in it that allowed me to attack forward and it was fine for the entirety of the game since the enemies come to you like I said and moving sideways and backward was more than enough to get them all. Since the boss can only be damaged by attacking forward while standing on the uppermost tile, I was cooked. I couldn't move there and attack it on the same turn and I would have taken a bunch of damage if I didn't move back right away since that's where the enemies spawn. This could definitely use a redesign since it hoses any sort of playstyle that doesn't have sufficient forward movement, which is discouraged throughtout the game as, like I said, forward is where enemies spawn so you tend to not want to stand there. I would suggest allowing the player to move back to the bottom when they try moving forward at the top of the map. Despite all the negatives, the game is fun, the music is amazing, the presentation of the world and its inhabitants is fantastic. Please hire an English voice actor (or two actually, it's literally the same guy voicing everything). I got it when it was 50% off but I think it's priced correctly for what it is even without the discount.

I'm still honestly a little confused about where I stand with regards to Takara Cards. On the one hand, the game has a few positives- I love the art, adore the music, the gameplay is really entertaining but simple- I think, for a roguelike, it has a lot of potential. The lore is also really interesting, I like the usage of standard fantasy races and I like the way that it portrays it's world. You can tell a lot of love and care went into the game. The core of what's here is really good and I really like it. However, there's a few weird things in the game that set me off just a bit. To start, the tutorial is very long. You do essentially 3 (or maybe it was 4?) battles, back to back, with little changing after the first. I think, as it is mandatory, shortening it in length would be very wise- it gave me the impression initially that this would be how long [i] every [/i] battle would be, and they're much shorter and much more fun. It definetly gave me the wrong first impression of the game. I also don't really get why it's mandatory- but it's fine I suppose. The second issue comes with character creation. You can play as one race at the start- this is very standard when it comes to roguelikes, you unlock more customization as the game progresses. That's very normal. However, the races are all unlocked with 1 playthrough- each is tied to the three bosses you play, so it's less "I'm limited to what races I can play throughout the game" and more "You can only play dwarf at the start". Personally, the best fix I could suggest is to make the other races harder to obtain (Maybe runs vs dragons?), or just let them all be choosable. I would reccomend the former much more- it would help emphasize each race, and give you the opportunity to use one each run, or you could just do a lot of runs as your one dwarf guy. Beyond that, I also think the events could use some work- Once, I did see an event that had some continuation in the little text box at the bottom but it was hard to read due to scrolling up being hard to do on that text box. Furthermore, they feel like their main purpose/function is to give you rep- I had a few events which led to things I saw later (A guy I saved thanked me) but for the most part I saw things then never saw them again. A much more specific note- Early on I had an event with mermaids where they asked me what I was doing, and I answered I was hunting dragons, assuming that was just the nice/social option. Later, I was reprimanded by the people who hired me and I didn't know why, so I said I was innocent. Later, on my reading of the codex, I noticed I was supposed to keep this secret because I was confused as to why they reprimanded me. I have a few suggestions with regards to this specifically, and I put it here because it relates to dialog: If I am lying or being untruthful, it should be shown (option could say (lie) maybe.) This one I was able to catch, but it might be harder to do so at other points. I should be able to check the codex during an event as well- this would let me check to see what I did wrong during the event instead of after. Alternatively, you could just mark the options like "oh you aren't supposed to do this" but I think that goes against the more playing-a-character aspect of the game. But my biggest issue easily comes with the final boss. (Spoilers, obviously.) [Spoiler] I have no idea what happened there even now. It started like a normal boss then it transitioned into dialog, and I started losing my perks at (seemingly) random intervals. I assumed this was a lead-in into me fighting them with little or no powers or abilities- but no, we just talked for a little bit and I got sent to the start because of a timeloop or w/e. I have no idea what really happened besides it telling me I needed more altruism in order to select certain dialog options- I'm assuming it's tied to certain levels of social stats (which it would really help if I could see the level I need a given stat to be for those dialogs). [/Spoiler] Additionally, it immediately threw me into the new game plus- I wasn't given the option to do it later or not do it at all. I could start it then go back to the menu and THEN delete the file, but it's still really weird that I can't just leave to the menu after beating the game and make the choice later. I would reccommend this game if you like small indie games with really interesting mechanics, I could see these issues being fixed / the game being refined later and becoming much better. In it's current state, it's a little confusing, but I could easily see this changing in the future. If you think these issues might hold you back from enjoying the game, I'd wishlist it and maybe look back in a week or two.

不好意思，第一眼看成了“太空宝批龙”。 原来是意译的Card宝卡和很有特色的音译Takara太空龙，因为真的在太空追逐巨龙！ 这是一款由Post Mortem Pixels制作的太空主题的卡牌构筑式类肉鸽游戏，由一家常年进行独立游戏发行的Grab The Games发行公司负责发行工作。 正巧如今是发行商特卖周末，其名下的作品每一款都非常有意思，均在折扣中。 另外，感谢牵线！ 这是一款太空开飞行器的游戏，如果拿到即时性的游戏中来，它就是一款不折不扣的弹幕式射击游戏《雷电》！ 有敌机，有导弹还有小行星，需要玩家躲避、攻击，最后杀出关卡！ 但它用了回合制的卡牌构筑肉鸽设计，通过卡牌和每一个回合的操作来进行上述即时进行的内容。 比如说，移位、换位、攻击或者攻击并撤退的卡牌作为行动方式，以每回合3格电池作为行动力来进行游玩。无论是小行星还是敌机，均会标记其血量和下一回合的行动方向，玩家只需要看好前方不可移动的区域有无障碍，在可移动范围内的敌方势力下回合如何移动，就能够准确的通过牌组清除、移动、规避下一回合的攻击。 直到前方再无障碍，就可以通过一回合的修正，满电的情况下跃出区域，通关。 飞船并非一次的攻击就会直接丧命，而是最初有着9条生命，这已经足够续命和推进更长一段距离了。即便是输了也不用担心回档重来，和大多数肉鸽游戏一样，它同样也有提升自己的养成玩法。 这是一款非常有想法的独立游戏，甜品级的肉鸽产品。值得体验一番！ [h1][quote] [table] [tr] [th] 欢迎关注 [b][u][i]网|易U_U鉴赏家培养计划[/i][/u][/b][/th] [/tr] [tr] [th] 关注网|易U_U加速器，开启精彩游戏之旅。 [/th] [/tr] [/table] [/quote][/h1]

Played for over an hour without enjoying any of it. Combat is way too simple and the rest of the game is not very well explained. Not sure what the overall motivation is to play. You toss your ship around a 3 x 3 grid for some reason to crash into other "enemies" with your shields to destroy them. There are attacks but it seems more geared to just using your ship to smash into things. I purposely destroyed my ship to see the outcome and it gives you an SOS ship to continue play. Um, no thanks, it wasn't fun in the first place. The game loop is boring and the story is uninteresting. There just isn't enough there to keep me interested. Maybe coming off an incredible game like Inkbound caused me to eye this game harshly but I can't see spending any more valuable gaming time on this rather tedious and lifeless venture.

Bought this game based on the store description, looking forward to a deckbuilding RPG. Should have checked the tags more carefully because the roguelike I got is both familiar and disappointing. The mechanics feel shallow and at times frustrating. The draw of a roguelike is usually being able to replay with varying builds and options, but I never felt like the cards in my deck changed my general strategy and usually just wished I had more consistent options. The loss of cards to extreme damage made the boss fights turn into death spirals or very long slogs without clear outs if they didn't go flawlessly. The RPG elements that exist feel underutilized or misplaced, the fact that the end of the game leans into them instead of the deckbuilding combat that is the core gameplay loop is confusing and underwhelming.

I have had a conflicted time with Takara Cards. I really enjoy the atmosphere and world the game sets up, and the mechanical foundations of the game are very solid. However, the game gets to be extremely repetitive extremely quickly. There is a distinct lack of enemy and encounter diversity, and it leads to the game feeling stale overtime. I would love to see some new enemy types and obstacles with different drawbacks / rewards. When I got to my act 2 boss and it was the same as the act 1 boss I basically lost all interest in the game. The node travel is fun, but the fact that you can visit every node on the map really drags out the travel segments. having to choose certain nodes and forgo others is a core strategic element for many rougelikes and its sorely lacking here imo. The UI while beautiful is also needlessly confusing, and while I definitely want to keep the flavor, I would appreciate more clarity in how elements are labeled in the UI. I think you definitely get used to it but it’s needlessly obtuse imo. The deckbuilding elements are kind of thin, there aren’t many cards with explicit synergies and the fact that you can’t upgrade cards (combined with the lack of enemy diversity) makes me feel like I’m not really progressing my deck in a meaningful way and instead am just filling it full of the best cards I can in every shop. Overall, really beautiful game with a really solid foundation for some very strategic gameplay, but I just don’t think it’s there yet.

"Not Quite the Adventure I Hoped For." Takara Cards makes a fantastic first impression. The visuals are vibrant and expertly crafted, with a style that immediately draws you in. Every area feels alive and thoughtfully designed. On top of that, the music pairs perfectly with the aesthetic, creating a really distinct vibe that makes the game feel special from the moment you hit “Start.” At first, the mechanics seemed deep and promising. The card-based movement across a grid is a clever idea, and I actually admired how different it felt compared to other deck-based games. There’s an interesting layer of planning involved—choosing which card to play just to position yourself correctly does add a puzzle-like element that initially kept me curious. But after about two hours, the cracks started to show. The game leans heavily on that movement mechanic as its primary gameplay loop, and over time it became repetitive instead of engaging. Most turns boil down to the same decision-making pattern: pick a card that matches the grid space you need, move, repeat. Once the novelty wears off, the experience starts feeling stale, and the sense of deeper strategy I expected never really materialized. The progression also didn’t do enough to keep me motivated. While the game offers choices and branching moments, the overall flow still felt limited. There were times I really wanted the mechanics to expand, evolve, or challenge me in new ways, but the gameplay stayed essentially the same for the duration of my run. Eventually, I realized I was forcing myself to push forward, hoping for a spark that never came. That said, I don’t think Takara Cards is a bad game — it’s just not for me. I can absolutely see a niche audience appreciating the unique movement system and the slow, methodical style. The developers clearly put a lot of love into the presentation and worldbuilding. But in my case, despite a strong start and some genuinely cool ideas, the gameplay loop just didn’t hold my interest long enough. I personally can’t recommend it, though I respect what it’s trying to achieve.

Needs a specific launch command to work in Steam Deck desktop mode without getting stuck on the launch screen, meaning if I want to play without being docked I need to modify launch commands, shouldn't have the "verified" tag in that case, this makes swapping between desktop and game mode really annoying. Overall the UI is the games worst problem, cards are stacked vertically instead of vertically unlike every single other deckbuilder so you have to mouse over them constantly, keywords are hidden in a glossary and even then not everything is explained you have to guess what keywords do as you can only check these things in between missions, if you encounter something while fighting, tough luck. Whenever you stop you have to go through each menu to figure out what you can actually do in each location, there are no visual indicators of what you can actually do, it feels more like navigating a terminal than choosing an option in a videogame. Everything in the game is just really unintuitive and hard to grasp, leading to constant friction and annoyance, I never felt like I was inching towards mastery, just figuring out the bizzare moon logic and what the game actually wants from me. Some enemies will say they are attacking but its not obvious where they are going to attack, and other enemies push things around so I got hit by random attacks that I thought I was safe from, extremely frustrating. Cards are far too restrictive, sometimes an enemy will warp in an inconvenient place and your draws will have no way to address them, leading to non turns, but this happens far too frequently, meaning lots of down time. Turns also take far too long to complete, so not only are some turns non-events, you also have to sit through these filler turns quite often. The selections in random events some times don't make sense, for instance because I had the "rich" karma I could pay off my debts instantly but I was already in debt, is it family inheritance, did I call in a favor? Who knows, its not really explained. At best the game could be seen as a vibes based experience, as the aesthetics, art and soundtrack are by far the best part of the game. Overall the game is just too ambitious for its limited scope and budget, instead of honing a small subset of features to perfection it feels like a grab bag of "this sounds cool, implement it", honestly I tried getting a refund but I was outside the 14 day window just for the launch command issue. The main thing that this game highlights is that for a card game playability, intuitive UI and easy to grasp hard to master concepts are essential otherwise you will bounce off quickly. I would stay far away even on a deep sale.

This game is sweet, simple but challenging gameplay. A recommend. Takara Cards does many things right. This is a simple card battle in a grid-based battlefield. There are many things could influence your card, like karma and equipment so even with the same card it could give you different result based on RNG. You improve your karma by interacting with the world at each stop after each battle. Each starting race also offers unique playstyle so if you get bore in 1 character you could create another for unique feels. The art design of this game is phenomenal, from simple enemies drones to character avatar, from sector's environment to cockpit's view. The music of this game is also S tier chilling slap. I even recommend you buy the soundtrack to chill outside of gaming. The game content is too short. While it could be endless because of roguelite nature of the game, but it took you about 10 hrs to see all it is in the game. This may not be a con for many, but this game could be so much more with its various system in place.
